where: Section 1, paragraph 3 ("The two chain directions are not identical because the chain has a repeat pattern.")
problem: The reason given is the opposite of the truth. A regular repeat pattern is exactly what makes the two chain directions constitutionally identical: walking left or right from the CHX carbon you meet the same –CH₂–CHX– sequence. A repeat pattern cannot be the reason the two groups differ. If students take this sentence literally, they cannot see why the CHX carbon is a stereocentre at all, and they will think any regular chain automatically creates one.
fix: At the CHX carbon, the fourth group besides H and X is the chain itself, taken in each direction. In a real chain the two ends are not the same (different end groups, different lengths, and a different R/S sequence further along), so the two chain directions count as two different groups. The CHX carbon therefore has four different groups and is a stereocentre. In an idealised endless regular chain the two directions are constitutionally identical, which is why some syllabi call this a pseudoasymmetric centre; the configurational argument still holds once end groups and the configurational sequence are counted.
